Subject: CAIQ / SIG evidence request — encryption & KMS

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call today. AlderBank's security team is pulling together the CAIQ/SIG packet for our vendor review and we need a compact evidence bundle covering encryption and key management. Can you provide the following by EOD Friday (2029-06-14)? If a full set isn't possible, a minimal extract plus an ETA is fine.

Specific asks: 
- HSM/KMS attestation or vendor statement (latest) with firmware/attestation date
- Key rotation logs for the past 90 days (operator id, rotate timestamp, key id, action) — sanitized is acceptable
- Evidence of separation-of-duties for HSM operators (shift logs or operator matrix)
- TLS configuration summary used for service-to-service and ingress (cipher suites, TLS versions)
- Evidence of at-rest encryption (algorithm, storage layer, key wrapping approach) and sample encrypted object metadata (no customer plaintext)
- Any CAIQ mapping or SIG rows you can pre-populate related to CRYPTO/ENCRYPTION

Delivery preferences: encrypted zip to security@alderbank.com or a shared Drive link; please flag any items requiring redaction.

Thanks — if we can get an initial package or a plan today that would help unblock procurement.

Claire Benton
Senior InfoSec Analyst — AlderBank
security@alderbank.com

Claire / team — attaching the initial artifacts and a short technical summary. See attachments: redwood_hsm_attestation_2029-05.pdf (vendor attestation), rotation_log_sample_2029-05.csv (sanitized sample), tls_config_snippet.txt (short TLS notes).

Technical summary (high level):
- HSM / KMS: We use AcmeHSM X7 (FIPS 140-2 Level 3 certified) for master KEKs. Latest vendor attestation signed 2029-05-11, firmware baseline v7.4.2 (attestation included). Root keys are split via 3-of-5 ceremony for escrow; HSM access requires operator auth plus operator badge + centralized KMS policy for key export blocking.

- Rotation cadence:
  * Data encryption keys (DEKs) — rotated per-tenant on a rolling 30–90 day cadence depending on workload; DEK rotation events are logged and the sample CSV includes columns: timestamp_utc, key_id, action, actor_hash, rotation_reason.
  * KEKs (wrapping keys) — rotated quarterly; KEK rotations are performed during maintenance windows and require dual-operator approval.

- Operator separation / shift logs:
  * Operator matrix (attached within attestation) shows distinct operator roles (operator, approver, auditor).
  * Shift logs have been hashed for operator identifiers; hashes are stable across the sample so you can map distinct operators without us revealing PII.

- At-rest encryption: AES-256-GCM for object stores; keys are wrapped with KEK (RSA-OAEP / AES-KW per CAIQ rows) before archival. We do not store plaintext keys in backups. Metadata we can provide: object_id, key_id_hash, envelope_algorithm, last_rotation_ts.

- In-transit / TLS: Service ingress uses TLS 1.3 preferred, fallback to TLS 1.2 where required. Preferred cipher suites: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384. We also enforce HSTS and mTLS for control-plane RPCs between regional services. Snippet attached.

- Redaction guidance: We replaced operator IDs with stable SHA256 hashes, removed internal IPs and request payloads. If AlderBank needs complete operator IDs for a third-party audit, we'll provide them under a scoped data access agreement.

Attachments:
- redwood_hsm_attestation_2029-05.pdf (HSM vendor statement, firmware/attest date visible)
- rotation_log_sample_2029-05.csv (sanitized — columns: timestamp_utc,key_id,action,actor_hash,notes)
- tls_config_snippet.txt (cipher suite list + mTLS note)

If you want a short readme that maps each attachment to CAIQ/SIG control IDs, we can add that by tomorrow.

— Irene Choi
Sr. Applied Cryptography Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwoodinference.com
